prompt: Write a note to a friend about garden tools that never seem to work. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hey Sam,

I need to vent about my garden tools, because I'm convinced they're conspiring against me.

Let's start with the hose. I bought a "kink-resistant" one last spring, and it has kinked in every spot I've tried to water. I'll be halfway across the yard, the flow dwindles to a sad trickle, and I have to trudge back and untwist it. The spray nozzle isn't any better. It has seven settings, and none of them is "water the plants without soaking your shoes." The trigger also leaks at the joint, so my sleeve is permanently damp.

Then there are the pruning shears. They were sharp for about two weeks. Now they chew through branches instead of cutting them, and the spring has gone limp, so they stay open like a bored mouth. I oiled them and sharpened them, and I even watched a video about it. They're still terrible. I've started cutting things with the kitchen scissors, which feels wrong, but at least it works.

The wheelbarrow deserves its own paragraph. The tire loses air at a steady rate, so every time I need it, it's flat. I've pumped it up, patched it, and finally replaced the tube. It's flat again. I suspect it knows when I'm in a hurry. Also, one handle has a loose bolt that tightens only to loosen again, so loads tend to lurch sideways at the worst moment. Last weekend I dumped half a load of mulch on the path instead of the bed.

And the trowel! I snapped the first one on a perfectly ordinary rock. The replacement bent like a spoon in hot soup. Now I'm using a cheap metal one that's too heavy and has blisters-in-waiting written all over the handle.

I know the standard advice is to buy better tools and spend more. I tried that with the loppers, and they jammed on day three. So apparently price isn't the answer either.

Anyway, I'm not giving up. The tomatoes did well despite everything, which feels like a small miracle. If you have any tools that have never let you down, please tell me the brand. Or just come over and laugh at me while I fight the hose. I'll make lemonade, and I promise the pitcher works.

Talk soon,
[name]
